items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: So when Chano came in he just mixed in with Diz and that’s the marriage with jazz and Latin see?

ctx.x: Someone wrote a review about you and your recordings and it says, “As clave conscious as he may be he has never been content with just being a timekeeper, nor does he look to hog the solo spotlight all for himself.” So it sounds like just what you’re talking about.

Yes. Because that happens with my quintet, a lot of people come to me and say, “You let these guys shine.” I lay out sometimes because I have a Latin jazz quintet but I consider my group jazz-Latin. It’s a jazz band with congas. That’s how I approach. Because once you hear “Latin music,” they think you’ve got a singer, it’s a salsa band, so Latin jazz is a whole genre in itself. One guy on a radio station asked me, “Do you think Latin jazz is a legitimate genre?” I said, “What.” I said okay. Well who’s the…
So what’s it like to make a living as a musician in New York City. Do you have to wear lots of hats?
